label: NYDFS Cybersecurity Regulation 23 NYCRR 500.17
authority: New York State Department of Financial Services (Superintendent)

sources.title: 23 NYCRR 500.17 Notices to superintendent, Cornell LII

statusNote: Applies to entities licensed or authorized under the New York banking, insurance or financial services laws. Notice of an extortion payment is due within 24 hours of the payment and a written explanation within 30 days.

triggers.label: Cybersecurity incident determined to have occurred
triggers.hint: The covered entity determines that a reportable cybersecurity incident has occurred at the covered entity, its affiliates or a third-party service provider.

triggers.label: Extortion payment made
triggers.hint: A payment is made to a threat actor in connection with a cybersecurity event.

clocks.label: Notice to the Superintendent
clocks.rule: Notify as promptly as possible and in no event later than 72 hours after determining that a cybersecurity incident has occurred.

clocks.label: Notice of an extortion payment
clocks.rule: Notify within 24 hours of the extortion payment.

clocks.label: Written explanation of the extortion payment
clocks.rule: Provide a written description of why the payment was necessary, the alternatives considered and the sanctions diligence conducted, within 30 days of the payment.

appliesTo.note: Entities licensed or authorized by the New York Department of Financial Services (banks, insurers and other financial services companies).
